Captain Thomas Best in 1612 A.D. dissolved the Portuguese monopoly with the victory at Swally. Consequently, the British established a permanent factory in 1613 A.D. s: Blue Water Policy is associated with
x:
The Blue Water Policy (Política da Água Azul) was introduced by the Portuguese Viceroy Francisco de Almeida, the first Portuguese Viceroy in India. The main objective of this policy was to establish Portuguese naval supremacy in the Indian Ocean rather than acquiring extensive inland territories. Almeida believed that control over the sea routes would enable Portugal to dominate the lucrative spice trade between Europe and Asia. To implement this policy, the Portuguese developed a strong navy, built coastal forts and attempted to eliminate Arab and other European competitors from maritime trade. Although Almeida emphasized naval supremacy, his successor Afonso de Albuquerque shifted Portuguese policy towards territorial expansion by capturing Goa, Malacca and Hormuz. Hence, the correct answer is Option (1).

• Successor – Afonso de Albuquerque
• Aim – Control of Indian Ocean trade

What was the headquarters of the Dutch East India Company's establishments in India?

The Dutch East India Company (VOC) was established in 1602 to conduct trade in Asia. Initially, the Dutch established trading factories at Masulipatnam, Pulicat, Nagapattinam, and other ports.
